_provenance: 40 rows from the T4 calibration sweep of 2026-09-15, emitted by `scripts/measure.py --json` via `scripts/calibration_sweep.py` and archived from the notebook's runs.zip. ONE Kaggle session, one stack: Tesla T4 (sm_75, 14,912 MiB), torch 2.14.0+cu130 / transformers 5.17.0 / peft 0.20.0, torchvision and torchaudio UNINSTALLED (the image shipped a torchvision built against a different torch, so `import transformers` died on `operator torchvision::nms does not exist`; nothing here measures an image model). `measured.cuda_context_mib` is 140.875 on all 40 rows, which is how you can tell they are one session. LoRA r=32 [q,k,v,o], fp16, AdamW fp32, gradient checkpointing ON for every row. 8 of the 40 are deliberate repeats of SmolLM2-1.7B bs=4 seq=1024 (suffix -r2/-r3, 3 per kernel per quant): they came back BIT-IDENTICAL, so the allocator noise floor on this card is zero and the 30.9% eager fragmentation is a mechanism, not variance. Exclude the repeats before fitting C_overhead or they carry 3x weight. The measured half is verbatim. The predicted half is recomputed with fitcheck 0.3.0: these rows are what identified the per-quantization activation profiles, so the predictions they were emitted with are the pre-correction ones and must not be reused. Measurements do not change when the formulas do. Each row also carries the `model_config` it was measured with, so the archive can be re-scored and re-fitted with no network access at all.
